But also
/sig architecture
^^ conformance tests may not be flaky

we can also see this in https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/e2e-ci-kubernetes-e2e-al2023-aws-conformance-cilium-canary/1859357552249147392

it looks like prow bugged out, it shows the run as completed if I click through:
https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-conformance-kind-ga-only/1858905568668815360

but on the overview page:
https://prow.k8s.io/?job=ci-kubernetes-conformance-kind-ga-only

that same job is showed as "running" ...
we can manually bypass that by triggering a re-run, but we should also log a bug with prow

One of the infra leads will probably have to poke around the underlying prow services cluster directly, the lack of results / stale tab is a bug with scheduling the job, the job itself isn't responsible for that and nothing changed with the config, something broke in the CI/prow.

(and this is unrelated to the flaking test, which is still a problem on its own)

... something eventually consisted and now I've manually requested a new run from the rerun UI.

That run is here and should have new results soon: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-conformance-kind-ga-only/1859760580349399040

So we can return this thread to: There seems to be a flake in this sig-scheduling test, which is extra bad because it's a conformance test.

> /remove-sig testing
This test is not failing in kind specifically, and we do not own tests, we own the test frameworks, CI, kind, etc.

/sig testing

Reapplying. This test is most likely failing due to the test framework change.
The patch is sent https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128954. sig-testing maintainers, please take a look.

review_comments: No need to retry I think. You can just do patch with status subresource.

But, you intentionally used the update, not patch, for ease here, right?
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128194#discussion_r1829913783

Yeah @AnishShah since you moved from Patch to Update, then you need to deal with possible conflicts client side

This LGTM too
Yeah. I thought there won't be resource conflict and hence used UpdateStatus. We can revert to patch again to avoid doing retry.

I meant, that was for the implementation simplicity, right?
I'm not sure why you prefer to switch back to the patch here. Efficiency-wise too, the flake is pretty rare, that is, the retry would happen only rarely, and I don't think we need to mind (... and this is a test code either way).
this is an e2e test so we don't need to over optimize, I think current approach is ok and avoids more code churn

> I meant, that was for the implementation simplicity, right? I'm not sure why you prefer to switch back to the patch here. Efficiency-wise too, the flake is pretty rare, that is, the retry would happen only rarely, and I don't think we need to mind (... and this is a test code either way).

patch requests avoid resource conflicts. so there won't be any need to retry and we can keep the logic simple and similar to `AddExtendedResource` func above.

either way works for me, I also prefer to use patch if the patch is really simple ... I'm just trying to say we should not overthink it, chose one solution and move on , a retry on conflict is common in multiple places of the code, so is nota bad solution either

We need either retry on update, or simply patch. Reported by @wendy-ha18 we got flakes and it's impacting 1.32 release: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C09TP78DV/p1733547680436909

Agree with @aojea we should move on either way. (we can follow-up with the approach of switching to patch)
